result.markdown: --- title: "Session 5 — External Validation, Decision Curves and Reporting" subtitle: "Transportability · calibration in a new district · model comparison · recalibration · net benefit · TRIPOD · Lab 5" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Sessions 1 to 4: build, evaluate, internally validate, shrink - Today: the **real test**: a **different district**, 2,000 adults, **never used for fitting** - By the end you can: - **validate externally** (discrimination, calibration) - **recalibrate** a model for a new setting - judge **clinical usefulness** with a **decision curve** - **report** with TRIPOD ::: # Topic 1 — Validation in a new district {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Discrimination and average calibration ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} roc_v <- roc(val$diabetes, val$risk, quiet = TRUE) c(auc = as.numeric(auc(roc_v)), predicted = mean(val$risk), observed = mean(val$diabetes)) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` auc predicted observed 0.709 0.179 0.246 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ci.auc(roc_v) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 95% CI: 0.6823-0.7358 (DeLong) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **AUC 0.71** (95% CI 0.68 to 0.74): **lower** than the apparent 0.80 and the bootstrap-corrected 0.776. **Mean predicted risk 17.9%** vs **24.6% observed**: the model **under-estimates** risk in this district (older, less active, higher prevalence). ::: ## Calibration slope and plot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(slope = coef(glm(diabetes ~ lpv, data = val, family = binomial))[["lpv"]], intercept_offset = coef(glm(diabetes ~ offset(lpv), data = val, family = binomial))[[1]]) |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` slope intercept_offset 0.67 0.50 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} calv <- val |> mutate(decile = ntile(risk, 10)) |> group_by(decile) |> summarise(predicted = mean(risk), observed = mean(diabetes)) ggplot(calv, aes(predicted, observed)) + geom_abline(linetype = 2) + geom_point(size = 3, colour = col_red) + geom_line(colour = col_red) + coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 0.7), ylim = c(0, 0.7)) + labs(x = "Mean predicted risk", y = "Observed proportion with diabetes") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s5_external_reporting_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Slope 0.67**: predictions are **too extreme** (low risks too low, high risks too high): some **overfitting** and **weaker effects** in the new district - **Intercept +0.50** (calibration-in-the-large): risk **under-estimated on average** - Typical of **external validation**: performance **drops** and **calibration** needs updating ::: ## Which development strategy transports best? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} slope_of <- function(lp) coef(glm(diabetes ~ lp, data = val, family = binomial))[["lp"]] lps <- list(ML_8 = predict(m_true, val), ML_all = predict(m_all, val), ridge = as.numeric(predict(cv_r, xv_all, s = "lambda.min")), lasso = as.numeric(predict(cv_l, xv_all, s = "lambda.1se"))) sapply(lps, function(lp) c(auc = auc_of(val$diabetes, lp), slope = slope_of(lp))) |> t() |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` auc slope ML_8 0.71 0.67 ML_all 0.69 0.53 ridge 0.70 0.80 lasso 0.71 1.59 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - The **all-markers** ML model is the **worst calibrated** (slope **0.53**) and has the lowest AUC (0.69) - **Ridge**: slope **0.80**, closest to 1 among the full models - **Lasso at λ.1se**: slope **1.59**: **over-shrunk** (too narrow) - **No strategy fully repairs** the change of population: that needs **recalibration** ::: # Topic 2 — Updating and usefulness {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Recalibration ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rec <- glm(diabetes ~ lpv, data = val, family = binomial) val$risk_rec <- predict(rec, type = "response") c(brier_before = mean((val$risk - val$diabetes)^2), brier_after = mean((val$risk_rec - val$diabetes)^2)) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` brier_before brier_after 0.170 0.165 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Recalibrate**: re-estimate the **intercept** (and the **slope**) in the new setting; keep the predictors and relative weights - **Brier 0.170 to 0.165**; the **AUC does not change** (only the calibration) - Better than **refitting everything** on a small local sample (overfitting), but needs **local outcome data** - Models need **updating over time** and across **settings** ::: ## Decision curve: net benefit ::: {.eq} net benefit = TP / n − FP / n × t / (1 − t) t = the risk threshold at which you would act ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} nb <- function(risk, y, t) { tp <- sum(risk >= t & y == 1); fp <- sum(risk >= t & y == 0); tp / length(y) - fp / length(y) * t / (1 - t) } ts <- seq(0.05, 0.40, 0.05) tibble(threshold = ts, model = sapply(ts, \(t) nb(val$risk_rec, val$diabetes, t)), treat_all = sapply(ts, \(t) mean(val$diabetes) - (1 - mean(val$diabetes)) * t / (1 - t))) |> mutate(across(-threshold, \(x) round(x, 3))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 8 × 3 threshold model treat_all 1 0.05 0.206 0.206 2 0.1 0.162 0.162 3 0.15 0.126 0.112 4 0.2 0.097 0.057 5 0.25 0.074 -0.006 6 0.3 0.063 -0.078 7 0.35 0.044 -0.161 8 0.4 0.027 -0.258 ``` ::: ::: ## Reading the decision curve ::: {.key} **Treat none = 0.** The model has the **same** net benefit as **treat-all** up to a threshold of **10%**, and a **clearly higher** one from **15%** (0.126 vs 0.112) up to 40%, where treating everyone becomes **harmful** (negative above about 25%). A net benefit of **0.10 at 20%** is like finding **10 extra true cases per 100 adults with no unnecessary test**. **Choose the threshold from costs and benefits**, not from the AUC. ::: ## Reporting: TRIPOD ::: {.good} - **Source of data**, setting, **outcome**, **predictors** and their measurement - **Sample size** and **events**; handling of **missing data** - The **full model** (**intercept and all coefficients**) so others can use it - **Performance**: AUC, **calibration** (plot, slope, intercept), with CIs - **Internal validation** (bootstrap) and **external validation**, any **updating** - **Limitations** and intended **use** (threshold, who) ::: ::: {.key} *Example:* "The model (logistic regression, 8 predictors, 84 events in 700 adults) had an apparent AUC of 0.80 (bootstrap-corrected 0.78); in an external cohort of 2,000 adults the AUC was 0.71, the calibration slope 0.67 and risk was under-estimated (mean 17.9% vs 24.6% observed)." ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 5 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `prediction-workshop/labs/lab5_external.R` - apply the model to the new district: AUC, calibration - compare ML, ridge and lasso; recalibrate - decision curve and a TRIPOD sentence ::: **Time:** 45 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p5q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="xax11m.pdl4ag" data-show="QSBkaWZmZXJlbnQgY2FzZS1taXggYW5kIHdlYWtlciBwcmVkaWN0b3IgZWZmZWN0cywgcGx1 cyBzb21lIG92ZXJmaXR0aW5n" data-explain="RXh0ZXJuYWwgdmFsaWRhdGlvbiB1c3VhbGx5IHNob3dzIGxvd2VyIHBlcmZvcm1hbmNlIGJl Y2F1c2Ugb2Ygb3ZlcmZpdHRpbmcgYW5kIGJlY2F1c2UgdGhlIG5ldyBwb3B1bGF0aW9uIGhh cyBhIGRpZmZlcmVudCBjYXNlLW1peCBvciBkaWZmZXJlbnQgcHJlZGljdG9yIGVmZmVjdHMu "} The AUC is 0.80 in development and 0.71 in the external cohort. What is the most likely reason? - The external cohort is larger, and large cohorts give lower AUCs - The model was fitted to the external cohort and is therefore too optimistic - AUC values cannot be compared between cohorts - A different case-mix and weaker predictor effects, plus some overfitting ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p5q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="xaxea8.pdlirq" data-show="UG9vciBjYWxpYnJhdGlvbi1pbi10aGUtbGFyZ2U6IHJpc2sgaXMgdW5kZXItZXN0aW1hdGVk IGluIHRoaXMgZGlzdHJpY3Q=" data-explain="QSBtZWFuIHByZWRpY3RlZCByaXNrIGJlbG93IHRoZSBvYnNlcnZlZCBwcmV2YWxlbmNlIG1l YW5zIHRoZSBtb2RlbCB1bmRlci1lc3RpbWF0ZXMgcmlzayBvbiBhdmVyYWdlLiBUaGlzIGlz IGEgZGlmZmVyZW50IHByb2JsZW0gZnJvbSBwb29yIHJhbmtpbmcgb3IgdG9vLWV4dHJlbWUg cHJlZGljdGlvbnMu"} The mean predicted risk is 17.9% and the observed risk 24.6% in the external cohort. What does this show? - Poor calibration-in-the-large: risk is under-estimated in this district - Poor discrimination: the model cannot rank the adults correctly - Good calibration, because both numbers are in the same range - Overfitting in the development data, which the calibration slope measures ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p5q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="xaxriy.pdlx94" data-show="UHJlZGljdGlvbnMgYXJlIHRvbyBleHRyZW1lOiBsb3cgcmlza3MgdG9vIGxvdywgaGlnaCBy aXNrcyB0b28gaGlnaA==" data-explain="QSBzbG9wZSBiZWxvdyAxIHNob3dzIHRoYXQgdGhlIHByZWRpY3RlZCByaXNrcyB2YXJ5IG1v cmUgdGhhbiB0aGUgdHJ1ZSByaXNrcy4gU2hyaW5raW5nIHRoZSBsaW5lYXIgcHJlZGljdG9y IGJ5IHRoZSBzbG9wZSB3b3VsZCBmaXggdGhpcy4="} What does an external calibration slope of 0.67 mean? - Risks are under-estimated by 33% for all of the patients in the cohort - Predictions are too extreme: low risks too low, high risks too high - The model gets two thirds of the patients right in the new cohort - The AUC is 0.67 in the validation cohort and 0.80 in development ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p5q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="xay4rp.pdmbqj" data-show="VG8gc2hvdyB0aGUgbmV0IGJlbmVmaXQgb2YgdGhlIG1vZGVsIGF0IGRpZmZlcmVudCByaXNr IHRocmVzaG9sZHM=" data-explain="QSBkZWNpc2lvbiBjdXJ2ZSB3ZWlnaHMgdHJ1ZSBwb3NpdGl2ZXMgYWdhaW5zdCBmYWxzZSBw b3NpdGl2ZXMgYXQgdGhlIHRocmVzaG9sZCB3aGVyZSBhIGNsaW5pY2lhbiB3b3VsZCBhY3Qs IGFuZCBjb21wYXJlcyB0aGUgbW9kZWwgd2l0aCB0cmVhdGluZyBldmVyeWJvZHkgb3Igbm9i b2R5Lg=="} What is a decision curve used for? - To plot the ROC curves of several different cohorts together on one graph - To find the risk threshold that gives the highest AUC for the model - To compare the calibration slopes of competing models in one picture - To show the net benefit of the model at different risk thresholds ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p5q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="xayi0b.pdmq7t" data-show="VGhlIGZ1bGwgZXF1YXRpb24gd2l0aCB0aGUgaW50ZXJjZXB0LCBhbmQgaG93IGl0IHdhcyB2 YWxpZGF0ZWQ=" data-explain="VFJJUE9EIGFza3MgZm9yIHRoZSBjb21wbGV0ZSBtb2RlbCBzbyB0aGF0IHJpc2tzIGNhbiBi ZSBjYWxjdWxhdGVkIGJ5IG90aGVycywgdG9nZXRoZXIgd2l0aCBpdHMgcGVyZm9ybWFuY2Ug YW5kIHZhbGlkYXRpb24u"} Which item is essential in a report of a model that others will want to use? - The full equation with the intercept, and how it was validated - The p-value of each predictor in the final model, with its estimate - The software code that was used to draw the ROC curve in the paper - The name of the statistician who developed the model and their institute ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **External validation** = the real test: AUC drops, calibration shifts - Report **calibration-in-the-large**, **slope** and a **calibration plot** - **Recalibrate** for a new setting; update over time - **Decision curve**: net benefit at the thresholds that matter - **TRIPOD**: full equation, performance, validation, limitations ::: **Next:** Cheat sheet and the next module

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
